text:
alice: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the embeddings/reranker endpoint after yesterday's kernel selection patch. p95 spiked across the board for small non-chat requests.
ben: Ugh. Do you have numbers?
alice: Quick snapshot from infra perf job:
```
before: p50=22ms p95=48ms p99=120ms qps=1800 kv_hit=0.62
after:  p50=28ms p95=95ms p99=310ms qps=1400 kv_hit=0.60
```
alice: Same traffic (reranker, short sequences ~8-32 tokens). looks like kernel change favored longer sequences but hurts tiny-batches.
carmen: That matches my profiling — kernel selection moved to fused-matmul kernel which has higher launch/warm latency for small seq lengths.
dave: Any changes to batching heuristics too? continuous batcher configs?
alice: We did tweak continuous batching to reduce tail latency overall by increasing max_batch_ms from 40->60, but that actually increased wait time for small items when queue depth low.
elain: (cc @ben) I think two interacting things: kernel overhead + batch formation policy that groups dissimilar token counts causing padding overhead and ineffective packing.
ben: For reranker/embeds (non-chat) workloads we should bias batch formation toward size-based bucketing rather than chronological sliding windows. small, deterministic token counts allow deterministic buckets.
elaine: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) revert kernel selection heuristic for short seqs (force legacy small-seq kernel), 2) add token-budget target per batch and smoothing so we don't exceed token budget while waiting too long, 3) reduce max_batch_ms for endpoints labeled "concatable-short".
carmen: I ran an experiment locally on dev box with token-budget target=512 and token-smoothing alpha=0.3 (EMA of token size). Results:
```
policy: {
  token_budget_target: 512,
  max_batch_ms: 25,
  max_batch_size: 64,
  queue_age_limit_ms: 150,
  bucket_by_token_length: true
}
before_qps=1800 p95=95ms
after_qps=1750  p95=52ms
```
ben: Nice. Can you paste the token-smoothing pseudo?
carmen: Sure:
```
# per-queue EMA of tokens_per_req
tokens_ema = alpha * last_tokens + (1-alpha) * tokens_ema
# target tokens in batch = tokens_ema * expected_batch_count, clipped to token_budget_target
```
dave: Sounds reasonable. Also KV cache behavior — reranker path currently disables prefix KV cache because inputs are short and mostly unique, but the change made us skip small-KV optimizations. Any profiling?
alice: KV hit rate basically unchanged ~0.6 -> 0.60, but the extra kernel overhead masked wins from caching. If we fix kernel selection for small seqs, caching effects should reappear.
elaine: For rollout plan: create a new batching policy variant `embeds-smallseq-v2` applied to reranker endpoints only, with: bucket_by_token_length=true, token_budget_target=512, max_batch_ms=25, queue_age_limit_ms=150. Canary at 5% traffic for 24h, monitor p50/p95/p99, qps, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV hit rate.
ben: Suggest also adding queue backpressure metric and avg_wait_ms and expose per-bucket metrics.
alice: I'll open a quick PR with the policy and a canary config. Also adding a short-term revert flag for the kernel selector for seq_len<=48.
dave: Can we get a microbenchmark script to reproduce locally? Might help perf team iterate quicker.
carmen: Pasted a tiny script for the dev perf runner:
```
# run_em.py
for n in range(1000):
  send_request(model='embed-small', tokens=random.choice([8,16,24,32]))
  sleep(0.003)
```
Use --concurrency 32 and collect p50/p95.
elaine: I'll wire alerts: delta_p95 > 20ms or qps droop >10% triggers auto rollback. :warning:
ben: Good. Also leave a note for runtime team about kernel selection heuristics — we need a cost model that includes launch overhead for short seqs, not just FLOP efficiency.
alice: Agreed. I'll include profiling traces (triton timeline + nvtx) in the PR. Anyone object to the canary plan?
dave: +1
carmen: +1
elaine: +1
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary-config/embeds-smallseq-v2 weight=5% TTL=24h
alice: Thanks all — will follow up with numbers after canary runs. :thumbsup:
